quotes.text: Customers must authorize the payment within three minutes. If authorization expires, the PaymentIntent returns to `requires_payment_method`. Successful PaymentIntents transition to `succeeded`.
Swish refunds are asynchronous. Stripe tracks the refund until Swish reports whether it succeeded or failed.
For payments processed through PPRO, Stripe sends this reference to PPRO as the statement descriptor. PPRO or the customer’s bank might display a different value on the bank statement.
The payment provider returns this identifier, which differs from the custom reference you set in `payment_method_options[swish][reference]`.

old_evidence.text: For Swish payments, Stripe operates as the merchant of record.

findings: May and November overview preserve single-use real-time Swish, Swedish customer, SEK currency, same 27 business-account countries, mobile redirect vs desktop QR, Swish app plus Swedish BankID approval, immediate success/failure notification and standard payout (old 8–56,58–88,98–116; new 9–20,36–94,195–227). November adds B2C only and domestic/cross-border, explicit SEK 3.00–150,000.00, plus portal access labels. New 14 says instant provisional access, while 22–32 provides email request and swish_beta_preview identifier, and 110 routes eligibility to Dashboard. Preserve both and avoid proving GA, universal access or need of identical request for every account.

The November overview adds the three-minute customer authorization window and PaymentIntent outcomes to this overview (new 195–227): expiry returns to requires_payment_method; success transitions to succeeded. The 2026-05-06 acceptance guide already gave the same production limits and state transitions, distinguishes completion from returning to the merchant using server-side webhook fulfillment, and describes method detachment when a requires_action payment expires (raw/stripe-swish-accept-payment-2025.md 914–926,984–988). The same May guide allows up to 20 QR refreshes in the Elements desktop path only (665–681). May test examples at 958–980 separately demonstrate test states. BankID and customer app return alone do not establish payment success or funds availability.

New 41–78 adds coded prohibited vs restricted categories, with 9 prohibited and 22 restricted rows and additional information at account creation for restricted MCCs. New 95–110 also retains May's non-exhaustive ten-entry prohibited list (old 137–152), including precious stones/metals/jewelry and wallet top-ups absent as named table rows. Preserve both; do not clear a category based on row omission. Current source 33 omits coded distinctions.

The new matrix affirms full page, Payment Links, embedded form, Payment Element, in-app, Connect, Checkout Sessions and PaymentIntents; rejects Express Checkout Element, Managed Payments, Billing, Invoicing, Customer Portal, Radar, Terminal, setup_future_usage, SetupIntents and Checkout setup/subscription modes (new 155–193). Old 90–96 and 127–131 support core frontends and Payment Links, alongside Connect charge types old 158–164. Old source lines 29–31 reflect method-only view. Both May and November extra real-time matrices mark Payment Links unsupported and Subscriptions supported only via send_invoice but Invoicing unsupported (old real-time 24–32; November real-time 25–34). Preserve the Payment Links/Billing tension and correct concept 36's claim that Swish Invoicing is supported via send_invoice. The cross-method matrix does not establish recurring or automatic collection.

May and November preserve no manual capture, no recurring, no standard disputes and 365 days after completion for full/partial and cumulative partial refunds within amount (old 30–52,154–156; new 112–153). November separately prohibits partial, multi, over-capture and listed authorization adjustments; it documents customer concerns handled directly, asynchronous refund tracked until provider result, Dashboard/Refund status and events, failed refund restores Stripe balance and merchant must use another method. November summary window says 1 year with blank processing time, but prose explicitly says up to 365 days and usually a few minutes (new 128–149). Keep precise prose and avoid guaranteeing timing.

Stripe remains merchant of record and its name appears as Swish app recipient and described bank descriptor; factoring addendum remains (old 54–56,133–135; new 18–20,237). November distinguishes the automatically populated Swish Message field (legal name then displayable name fallback, destination on_behalf_of uses connected account name, filtered/truncated to 50), custom 1–35-character letters/numbers/hyphens reference, PPRO-specific descriptor forwarding with possible different display, and provider-returned bank reference under expanded latest_charge.payment_method_details.swish.payment_reference (new 229–243). General Connect descriptor ownership mapping does not control the Swish Message or PPRO mapping. The May acceptance guide says order reference is displayable in app (extra old 764–775), distinct from automatic Message and conditional PPRO output. Do not promise actual bank display. Source 23's old description needs these qualifications, and old 158–164/new 185–193 retain Direct, Destination and Separate charges and transfers.

Old local screenshots at 102,108 change to CDN at new 212,217; product matrix restructuring and links are presentation except express capability cells and instructions. Both old 118–125 and new 245–249 retain Dashboard enablement or manual acceptance guide path. Linked implementation and legal pages are navigation unless actually read here.

source_assessments.reason: November materially adds activation and eligibility scope, the previously documented May acceptance three-minute lifecycle to this overview, explicit capabilities, MCC criteria, refund outcomes and reference/descriptor rules. Preserve and qualify older coverage, billing product conflicts and dated merchant-of-record inputs.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/swish, the November 7, 2026 capture describes single-use Swish for Swedish customers and SEK 3.00–150,000.00, domestic/cross-border B2C and the same 27 listed business-account locations as May. The merchant or Connect platform has a provisional-access label alongside an email request, and MCC eligibility applies. The customer goes to Swish by mobile redirect or desktop QR, authenticates with Swedish BankID and must authorize within three minutes. Expiry moves PaymentIntent to requires_payment_method and success to succeeded. Stripe immediately notifies the merchant of the outcome, with standard payout timing (old raw lines 8-56 and 58-116, new raw lines 9-94 and 195-227). Stripe remains merchant of record with factoring terms. November adds distinct Swish Message, conditional PPRO custom descriptor and provider-returned bank reference. Refunds may be partial or full within 365 days and are asynchronous with explicit failure recovery; customer concerns go to merchant directly. source-stripe-swish.md records the core May behavior but lacks these newer limits, status boundaries, coded restrictions and identifier qualifications. The separate real-time matrix has a Payment Links and send_invoice Subscriptions conflict (old raw lines 127-164 and new raw lines 112-193 and 229-243).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/swish, substantive November documentation adds provisional-access/request coexistence, B2C and cross-border coverage, amount limits, prohibited/restricted MCC distinctions, three-minute expiration and PaymentIntent states newly included in this overview, expanded product/API matrix, asynchronous refund status and identifier/descriptor details (old raw lines 8-56 and 127-164, new raw lines 9-110, 112-193 and 195-243). The May 6, 2026 acceptance guide already states the same three-minute limit, expiry/failure and success states, separate server-side webhook fulfillment, and method detachment after expiration from requires_action (raw/stripe-swish-accept-payment-2025.md lines 914–926 and 984–988). The 20-refresh condition belongs to the May Elements desktop QR path (lines 665–681). Preserve May's 27-market merchant scope separately from Sweden customers, standard payout, no recurring/capture/disputes and Stripe merchant-of-record and factoring terms. Retain the dated method-page Payment Links support versus the extra matrices’ unsupported cells, November method Billing/Invoicing exclusions versus matrix send_invoice-only Subscriptions, and the distinction between PPRO routing, Connect mapping and actual display. November screenshots/CDN, restructuring and linked acceptance are presentation/navigation. Update source-stripe-swish.md with exact 365-day prose and ordinary few-minute estimate, keep both dated raw routes, and preserve the root-to-Stripe index and reciprocal Real-Time Payments concept/source links alongside separate acceptance and matrix references.
